newsitem.title: UK: Surgut sees no need for Western partners.
newsitem.headline: Surgut sees no need for Western partners.

text.p: Russian oil giant Surgutneftegaz is not looking for strategic partners in the West and prefers to borrow from Russian commercial banks, a senior company official said on Tuesday.

"At the moment our projects are financed 80 percent from our own sources and 20 percent from bank credits," Vladislav Barankov, Surgut's deputy general for economics, told reporters during a conference on investing in Russia.
"The conditions are more favourable and we make use of this."

He said even if Surgutneftegaz, one of the top three oil companies in Russia, increased its borrowing it would not reach a critical mass that would require it to surrender independence or look to the West.

Vladimir Bogdanov, president of Surgut Holding (NK Surgutneftegax) and chief executive of its main operating company AO Surgutneftegaz told the conference the firm saw itself as a regional company, albeit a powerful and successful one and had no plans at present to operate in the west.

Surgutneftegaz, based in western Siberia, produced about 666,000 barrels of crude oil per day in 1996 and expects to maintain that rate this year. It reported net profits last year of 1.9 trillion roubles, up from 1.8 trillion in 1995, the company said earlier this month.
Bogdanov said a planned new export terminal at Battery Bay on the Gulf of Finland would handle only oil products rather than crude.
Barankov said this project would also probably be funded with the help of Russian banks rather than through other channels.

LUKoil, the biggest of the dozen or so vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years, has a major joint venture agreement with Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO) of the United States.
Other western companies are interested in equity ownership and oil developments pojects with various other Russian oil firms.
